title: kv: burstless spill scheduler and soft-commit protector
author: Asha Nair
release_notes: Introduces a tenant-aware spill scheduler that smooths eviction-induced I/O and a soft-commit protection mechanism to reduce cache churn during hot batching windows. Opt-in via runtime knob: kv.spill.burstless=true. Backwards compatible; safe rollout with canary by tenant.
description:
Motivation: Under bursty load patterns (short hot tails from continuous batching + KV pressure) we observed large, sudden spill waves that caused latency spikes and cascading eviction churn across tenants. This PR implements a two-part mitigation: (1) a burstless spill scheduler that spreads spill work across a configurable window and applies tenant-aware pacing, and (2) a soft-commit protector which temporarily raises residency protection for pages that are part of in-flight batch kernels to avoid immediate re-eviction.

Design summary: The scheduler replaces the previous immediate spill trigger path with a reservoir-based token allocator. When pressure crosses the spill threshold, a per-node spill reservoir is populated proportional to pressure and redistributed to tenant buckets using their prioritization score (tenant SLA + recent throughput). Each tenant consumes tokens to perform spill operations; once tokens are exhausted further spill work is deferred into the next window. The scheduler supports two time scales: smoothing window (default 250ms) for latency-sensitive workloads, and background refill window (default 2s) for throughput catch-up.

Soft-commit protector: To reduce churn when continuous batching pipelines are flushing KV pages back to storage, we introduce a soft-commit state for pages touched by a batch. Pages in this state get a short-lived residency boost (configurable, default 500ms) and are gated from immediate eviction unless global memory danger is critical. The protector integrates with the continuous-batcher hook so that pages participating in a kernel or pinned by a streaming response are less likely to be reclaimed mid-flight.

Kernel and scheduling interactions: We added hint metadata to the KV allocator so the serving runtime can mark slots as batching-hot. The kernel scheduler checks these hints before preempting a GPU-bound batch to avoid introducing page faults during attention computation. This required a small knob in the kernel invocation path to consult the KV hint map (lightweight C++ API).

Telemetry and observability: New metrics: kv.spill.window_tokens_total, kv.spill.tokens_used_by_tenant{tenant}, kv.soft_commit.active, kv.soft_commit.eviction_blocked, kv.spill.deferred_ops. We added tracing spans around spill windows for correlating with request latency. Dashboards updated in observability-pack to show spill smoothing behavior and tenant pacing.

Configuration knobs: kv.spill.burstless (bool), kv.spill.smoothing_ms (int), kv.spill.refill_ms (int), kv.spill.tenant_share_strategy (enum: proportional|fair|sla_weighted), kv.soft_commit.duration_ms (int), kv.soft_commit.force_evict_threshold_pct (int). Defaults chosen to be conservative: smoothing_ms=250, refill_ms=2000, duration_ms=500, force_evict_threshold_pct=95.

Benchmarks: We ran mixed workload experiments on a 4x A100 dedicated cluster with representative continuous-batching trace and adversarial single-tenant fill. Key comparisons versus main branch: 
- 95th pct latency (inference tail) reduced from 182ms to 135ms under bursty injection (-26%).
- KV-induced stall events (page-fault stalls) reduced by 68% during hot tail windows.
- Background spill throughput decreased by ~12% in the short term (tradeoff for latency smoothing), but overall bytes spilled over 60s matched baseline due to refill windows.

Testing: Unit tests added for reservoir token accounting, tenant share strategy, and soft-commit state transitions. Integration test harness extended to simulate continuous batching with page affinity; deterministic scheduler tests added (non-flaky via mocked time). Load tests executed in benchmark-lab repo with the included scenarios.

Rollout plan: Feature is behind runtime flag (kv.spill.burstless). Default off for now; will be enabled for 10% of tenants via canary on the dedicated pool, monitor kv.soft_commit.eviction_blocked and inference tail. If stable after 72h, increase to 50% then flip default.

Commits summary: Implement reservoir allocator (kv/spill/reservoir.{h,cc}), tenant pacing policy, soft-commit state machine (kv/soft_commit.{h,cc}), kernel hint plumbing (runtime/kernel_hint.h), metrics and traces, unit/integration tests, docs and dashboard JSON.

Changed files (high-level):
- kv/spill/reservoir.cc
- kv/spill/reservoir.h
- kv/pacing/tenant_shares.cc
- kv/soft_commit.cc
- runtime/kernel_hint.h
- runtime/kv_integration_tests.cc
- observability/dashboards/kv_spill_smoothing.json
- benchmark-lab/scenarios/continuous_batch_spill.yml
- docs/kv_spilliness.md

Review thread (high level):
- Miguel Ortiz: "Nice approach. Concern: how do we avoid starving low-priority tenants when a tenant has sustained high pressure?"
- Asha Nair (author): "We cap per-tenant consumption and use proportional refill; added a hard min share to tenant_shares and tests to prevent starvation. See tenant_shares.cc lines 120-150."
- Priya Shah: "What about worst-case when memory pressure hits >95%? Do we bypass the smoothing?"
- Asha Nair: "Yes, config force_evict_threshold_pct defaults to 95; above that we switch to emergency mode where we bypass soft-commit protector and allow immediate evictions, and we emit kv.spill.emergency_count metric."
- Jonah Reed: "CI flaked on the deterministic scheduler test once; looks like clock mocking race."
- Asha Nair: "Fixed with stronger barrier in scheduler test and added a retry guard. Re-run CI."
- Miguel Ortiz: "Approved after test fixes and docs updates."

CI history: First run - unit failure (deterministic scheduler test) and lint warning. Fixes pushed (two commits). Second run - flaky integration test in perf harness (timeout); increased test timeout and optimized setup. Final run - all checks passed (unit/integration/lint/bench).

Merge: Squash merged by Asha Nair on 2025-02-19 (merge commit: 3f7b9a2). Merge note: Enable behind kv.spill.burstless; observability deck updated; benchmark manifests added to benchmark-lab.

Notes/Follow-ups:
- Follow-up ticket ENG-5060 to evaluate adaptive window sizing based on observed spike frequency.
- Consider integrating with autoscaler heuristics to preemptively increase memory reservations for tenants that consistently hit refill windows.

This PR is intentionally conservative: it prioritizes inference tail stability over immediate reduction in bytes spilled. It provides knobs for operators to tune the smoothing/refill tradeoffs and keeps a clear escape hatch for emergency evictions.
